chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq al-Talaqani (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Abdul-Aziz ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Dhubbi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Hilal narrated to us, saying: Na'il ibn Nujaih narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Shamar narrated to us, from Jabir al-Ju'fi, saying:

I asked Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (peace be upon them both) about the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: "like a good Tree whose root is firmly established and whose Branch is in Heaven? It brings its Fruit all the time, by the permission of its Lord."

He said: As for the Tree, it is the Messenger of Allah, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and its Branch is Ali (peace be upon him) and the twig of the tree is Fatima, the daughter of Allah’s Messenger (peace be upon him and his Family) and its Fruits are her sons, peace be upon them, and its Leaves are our party.

He, peace be upon him, then said: Indeed, a believer from our party is surely to die, and a leaf will fall from the Tree, and indeed, a newborn from our party is surely born and the Tree grows a leaf.
ai.seo_question: Who are the components of the 'Good Tree' in Surah Ibrahim according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Baqir elucidates the allegory of the 'Good Tree' (Surah Ibrahim: 24-25) by mapping its components to the Ahl al-Bayt, thereby establishing a cosmological hierarchy where the Prophet is the root, Ali the branch, Fatima the twig, and their progeny the fruit. This interpretation underscores the Shia doctrine of the spiritual vitality of the community, where the birth and death of believers are symbolically linked to the flourishing or shedding of leaves on this divine tree, emphasizing the inseparable connection between the Imams and their followers.
